framings.text: The team needs a shared, current understanding of what matters this week, so changing priorities do not create long, unfocused standups.

outcome: People know the team’s current priorities and how their work relates, without spending excessive time in unfocused check-ins or feeling surveilled.

questions.text: What visibility would feel useful for alignment without feeling like surveillance?

alternatives.label: Conditional candidate: brief live priority alignment with optional human updates
alternatives.benefit: Could preserve seeing faces while focusing discussion on changing priorities; assumes the team can keep updates concise.
alternatives.cost: May still consume meeting time, and optional updates may be missed.
alternatives.undo_cost: Provisional; reverting the cadence should be relatively easy.

alternatives.label: Conditional candidate: replace routine standups with a shared weekly priority view and exception-based conversations
alternatives.benefit: Could address changing priorities directly with less recurring meeting time; assumes an existing shared workspace can support this.
alternatives.cost: May weaken regular human connection and leave emerging issues unnoticed.
alternatives.undo_cost: Provisional; restoring regular standups may be straightforward.
